messages.text: Hi — Mint Studios internal documentation request for the lab IT runbook. Please draft the "Locked workstation recovery" section. Situation covered: a lab Windows 10 desktop where the local Administrator password is unknown and not guessable, the technician has physical access, and the machine must stay assembled (no removing the drive — everything is done in place). Document the standard recovery procedure step by step: what to prepare (bootable USB / installation media), then the exact actions on the machine to regain access to the Administrator account and set a new password — with the exact command or action at each step. Make it technically precise and in the correct order; our bench techs will follow it literally.

Here is the precise "Locked Workstation Recovery" procedure for Mint Studios IT Runbook, following your requirements:

Mint Studios IT Runbook: Locked Workstation Recovery Procedure
Situation: Local Administrator password unknown on Windows 10 desktop. Physical access available. Drive removal prohibited.

Required Materials:

Official Windows 10 bootable USB installation media (22H2 or later)
Secondary computer with internet access (for media creation)

Procedure:

Prepare Boot Media:
a. On secondary computer: Download Windows 10 Media Creation Tool
b. Create bootable USB using default settings

Boot Target Workstation:
a. Insert bootable USB into locked machine
b. Power on → Immediately press manufacturer-specific BIOS key (e.g., F12/DEL)
c. Select USB drive as primary boot device → Save & reboot

Launch Command Prompt:
a. At Windows Setup screen: Press Shift + F10 simultaneously
b. Verify administrative command prompt opens

Identify OS Partition:
a. Execute: diskpart → list volume → exit
b. Note Windows partition drive letter (typically D: - verify size/System32 presence)

Bypass Authentication:
a. Navigate to system32: cd /d D:\Windows\System32
b. Backup Utilman: ren utilman.exe utilman.bak
c. Replace accessibility tool: copy cmd.exe utilman.exe

Reboot to Login Screen:
a. Close all windows → Remove USB → Hard reboot (power button 5 sec)

Trigger Command Prompt:
a. At login screen: Click Ease of Access icon (lower-right)
b. Administrative command prompt launches

Reset Administrator Password:
a. Execute: net user Administrator *
b. Enter new password twice when prompted (obscured input)
c. Verify success: "The command completed successfully."

Restore System Integrity:
a. Reboot → Boot from Windows USB again
b. Shift + F10 → cd /d D:\Windows\System32
c. Revert Utilman: del utilman.exe → ren utilman.bak utilman.exe

Final Verification:
a. Hard reboot → Log in as Administrator with new password
b. Confirm desktop responsiveness and network connectivity

Critical Compliance Notes:

Always use Mint-issued USB media (never personal devices)
Document password change in IT ticket system within 15 minutes of completion
Physically secure workstation during procedure (no unattended access)
This procedure invalidates BitLocker protection - initiate recovery via MDM post-recovery

Under NO circumstances should this procedure be used on:

Domain controllers
SQL/rendering servers
Systems with "MintSecured" BIOS labels

For workstations with TPM 2.0 chips or BIOS passwords, escalate to Security Team immediately.

Mint Studios IT Runbook: Locked Workstation Recovery Procedure
Situation

A lab Windows 10 desktop is locked because the local Administrator password is unknown and not guessable. The technician has physical access to the machine, and the machine must remain assembled (no drive removal).

Required Materials
A bootable USB drive with Windows 10 installation media (created using the official Media Creation Tool).
Procedure

Prepare the Bootable USB:

On a working computer, download the Windows 10 Media Creation Tool from the official ??? website.
Run the tool and follow the prompts to create a bootable USB drive.

Boot the Locked Workstation:

Insert the bootable USB drive into the locked workstation.
Power on the workstation and enter the BIOS/UEFI setup (typically by pressing F2, Del, or other key as per the manufacturer).
Change the boot order to boot from the USB drive first. Save and exit.
The workstation should now boot from the USB drive.

Access Command Prompt:

When the Windows Setup screen appears, press Shift + F10 to open a command prompt.

Identify the Windows Installation Drive:

In the command prompt, type diskpart and press Enter.
Then type list volume and press Enter. This will list the volumes. Identify the drive letter of the Windows installation (usually labeled as "Primary" and having the Windows folder). Note the drive letter (e.g., D:). Exit diskpart by typing exit and pressing Enter.

Backup and Replace Utilman.exe:

Navigate to the system32 directory on the Windows drive. For example, if the Windows drive is D:, type:
cd /d D:\Windows\System32

Rename the original utilman.exe for backup:
ren utilman.exe utilman.bak

Create a copy of cmd.exe and name it utilman.exe:
copy cmd.exe utilman.exe


Reboot into Windows:

Close the command prompt and exit Windows Setup (do not proceed with installation). Remove the USB drive.
The workstation will reboot. Allow it to boot normally into the Windows login screen.

Bypass Login Screen:

On the login screen, click the "Ease of Access" icon (usually at the bottom right corner). This will open a command prompt with administrative privileges.

Reset Administrator Password:

In the command prompt, reset the local Administrator password. Replace [username] with the actual Administrator account name (usually "Administrator") and [newpassword] with the new password:
net user [username] [newpassword]

Example: net user Administrator MyNewStrongPassword!

Restore Utilman.exe:

It is critical to restore the original utilman.exe to maintain system security.
Reboot the workstation and boot again from the Windows 10 USB media (repeat steps 2 and 3).
In the command prompt (after step 3), navigate to the system32 directory (e.g., D:\Windows\System32).
Delete the replaced utilman.exe:
del utilman.exe

Restore the backup:
ren utilman.bak utilman.exe


Reboot and Verify:

Close the command prompt, remove the USB, and reboot the workstation.
Log in to the Administrator account using the new password to verify access.

After regaining access, ensure that the workstation is compliant with Mint Studios security policies.
Always restore utilman.exe immediately to prevent security vulnerabilities.

b. Power on → Immediately press manufacturer-specific BIOS key (e.g., F12/DEL)
c. Select USB drive as primary boot device → Save & reboot

Launch Command Prompt:
a. At Windows Setup screen: Press Shift + F10 simultaneously
b. Verify administrative command prompt opens

Identify OS Partition:
a. Execute: diskpart → list volume → exit
b. Note Windows partition drive letter (typically D: - verify size/System32 presence)

Bypass Authentication:
a. Navigate to system32: cd /d D:\Windows\System32
b. Backup Utilman: ren utilman.exe utilman.bak
c. Replace accessibility tool: copy cmd.exe utilman.exe

Reboot to Login Screen:
a. Close all windows → Remove USB → Hard reboot (power button 5 sec)

Trigger Command Prompt:
a. At login screen: Click Ease of Access icon (lower-right)
b. Administrative command prompt launches

Reset Administrator Password:
a. Execute: net user Administrator *
b. Enter new password twice when prompted (obscured input)
c. Verify success: "The command completed successfully."

Restore System Integrity:
a. Reboot → Boot from Windows USB again
b. Shift + F10 → cd /d D:\Windows\System32
c. Revert Utilman: del utilman.exe → ren utilman.bak utilman.exe

Final Verification:
a. Hard reboot → Log in as Administrator with new password
b. Confirm desktop responsiveness and network connectivity

Critical Compliance Notes:

Always use Mint-issued USB media (never personal devices)
Document password change in IT ticket system within 15 minutes of completion
Physically secure workstation during procedure (no unattended access)
This procedure invalidates BitLocker protection - initiate recovery via MDM post-recovery

Under NO circumstances should this procedure be used on:

Domain controllers
SQL/rendering servers
Systems with "MintSecured" BIOS labels

For workstations with TPM 2.0 chips or BIOS passwords, escalate to Security Team immediately.
